surface_mechanism_description: The reaction between TTIP and water involves two half-reactions: first, the surface hydroxyl groups react with the titanium precursor, releasing isopropoxide ligands. Second, the surface titanium species react with water molecules, releasing additional isopropoxide ligands and forming hydroxyl groups. At higher temperatures, surface hydroxyl groups combine to form water molecules, which are desorbed from the surface. The presence of plasma enhances the reaction by increasing the reactivity of oxygen plasma, leading to denser films and lower water vapor transmission rates.
evidence: The mechanisms of the reaction between TTIP and water were studied by Rahtu and Ritala 37 and Aarik et al .31 using deuterated water to identify them. It was found that between 150 and 250 /C14 C half of the isopropoxide ligands are released during the TTIP pulse in reaction with hydroxyl groups and the other half are released during the water pulse. The two half equations are 2 /C0 OD(s) + Ti(OCH(CH3)2)4(g) → ( /C0 O/C0 )2Ti(OCH(CH3)2)2(s) + 2(CH3)2CHOD(g); and ( /C0 O/C0 )2Ti(OCH(CH3)2)2(s) + 2D2O(g) → ( /C0 O/C0 )2Ti(/C0 OD)2(s) + 2(CH3)2CHOD(g);. For temperatures higher than 250 /C14 C, one isopropoxide group reacts with one surface hydroxyl group and the other three isopropoxide groups react with the water pulse. The reaction between O radicals and organic ligands produces H2O, CO, and CO2. Moreover, surface carbonates and bicarbonates are known to be formed due to simultaneous reaction of H2O and CO2 with a metal oxide surface.
